⭐ TWO PULL REQUESTS EXPORTED AGAINST THE SAME MAIN, AND MERGING THE FIRST SILENTLY BROKE THE SECOND'S LINEAGE WHILE GITHUB REPORTED IT `MERGEABLE / CLEAN` THROUGHOUT.

Measured 2026-08-26 on PRs #345 and #346. Both exported against the same committed export, `c7138a4f`. Merging #345 moved main's export to `fd93ff0b`, leaving #346's `prev_content_hash` pointing at a hash no commit on main held any more.

    before merging #345    main export = c7138a4f    #346 prev = c7138a4f    chain intact
    after  merging #345    main export = fd93ff0b    #346 prev = c7138a4f    CHAIN BROKEN
    git's opinion, both times: MERGEABLE / CLEAN

🛑 **GIT CANNOT SEE THIS AND NEVER WILL.** The two exports have no textual conflict — they are complete documents that merge cleanly — so every signal a forge offers stays green. The lineage chain lives INSIDE the file as a content hash, and only `reflow2_check`'s LINEAGE finding looks at it. Same class as `req:stale-seat-knows`: *a stale export is a COMPLETE document, so it merges cleanly and the missing work simply vanishes.*

⚠️ **THE CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY PROJECT RUNNING TWO PRs AT ONCE**, which is the general form and the reason this is worth keeping: `dec:export-once-per-pr` makes each branch export once, chained from main. **Two branches open simultaneously both chain from the same main, and whichever merges second is broken by the first.** Nothing warns at open time; the break appears only when the second branch's gate runs after the first merges. On a team this is the common case rather than the exception.

⭐⭐ **AND A CORRECTION WORTH MORE THAN THE FINDING: THE MERGE DRIVER REPAIRED THE LINEAGE, WHICH THE STANDING NOTE SAYS IT CANNOT.** The release-cut lore held that *"the three-way merge driver merges CONTENT correctly and cannot repair LINEAGE"* — recorded after a rebase needed a re-export. Rebasing #346 onto the new main on 2026-08-26 produced:

    reflow2: merged 3229 node(s) and 14029 edge(s) — 53 divergence(s) resolved automatically, no conflicts
    prev_content_hash after rebase: fd93ff0b   (== main's content_hash — REPAIRED)

The restore-from-main-and-re-export was still performed, because trusting an unverified repair on the one field the gate checks would be exactly the false-green habit this session hit five times. **But the driver did the right thing unprompted, and the note claiming otherwise is now wrong.** Whether it repairs lineage in every case or only when the branch's export is a superset is NOT established — one observation, one shape.

📌 VERIFIED AFTER THE REPAIR, three ways rather than assumed: `prev_content_hash` equalled main's `content_hash`; #345's `ver:graph-algorithms-unit-suite` survived the merge; exactly one commit on the branch touched the export.
